The crippling essence of the human condition, for most of us who have arrived here (if you don't belong here, run;) is that we aren't addicted to a particular drug. We aren't diseased, there's no magic pill or word or affirmation or shake, there's no way to "simply" think your way out of this.

Some people will always have the nagging need to change our state, because we're unhappy, we're unfulfilled with our life, maybe with all of what life has to offer in general. We're missing something that we can't describe but we just know should be there, it's something that other people have, maybe, or maybe just something they haven't noticed is missing but the fact that it can't quite be articulated (at least by me) doesn't mean that it isn't real. I don't want to fall back on trite analogies; it's not a hole we're trying to fill or a trauma that wasn't resolved. It's a raw, vicious existential dread which lives in the back of your mind, the part that you can never forget but can never let yourself think about if you value your sanity. That part of your mind exists, and all of the drugs in the world aren't going to change that.

I don't really like the addict/non-addict dichotomy but it's useful, if imperfect terminology. Addicts can become non-addicts, recover; addicts can be doing great things while addicts, there are people like you all around you that you might not even notice (and you don't miss a trick, right?) That's not what is missing though, and that is the intrinsic problem with the recovery paradigm, with the idea that addiction is as simple as some cause-effect-resolution, that you can take a twelve step stairway out. There is something essential missing in us, maybe only one thing, but whatever that thing is: we're never going to be to let it go until we find out what it is, why it bothers us, why it effects us the way that it does and everyone else seems willfully oblivious, just why?

Personally, until and unless I figure it out, I'm fine with getting through my days; getting high, with a little help, from my friends.

RAGS is one of a few game systems often utilised by game designers. It is free to use to both make and play games.

The games it produces are simple click and read, with images and a relatively diverse toolset for the player inventory, story progression and more.

Grab it here

You also need the Player to play the games made with RAGS, and herein lies a small caveat: versions.

RAGS Player does not have robust backwards compatibility, and often a game will have to be played in the specific version of the player it was made in (at time of writing I have two versions of the Player installed on my computer.) so be sure to check the game's version requirements.
